questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Oscillations, Waves and Optics (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A damped harmonic oscillator of natural angular frequency $\omega_0$ and damping parameter $\gamma < \omega_0 / \sqrt{2}$ is driven by a sinusoidal force $F_0 \cos(\omega t)$. Velocity resonance occurs at the driving angular frequency
questions.explanationEn: The steady-state velocity amplitude is $v_0(\omega) = \frac{F_0 / m}{\sqrt{(\omega - \omega_0^2/\omega)^2 + 4\gamma^2}}$, which is maximized when $\omega - \omega_0^2/\omega = 0$, i.e., $\omega = \omega_0$ (independent of damping).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Oscillations, Waves and Optics (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Linearly polarized light is incident normally on a quarter-wave plate. The emergent light is circularly polarized when the angle between the incident plane of polarization and the optic axis of the plate is
questions.explanationEn: A quarter-wave plate introduces a $\pi/2$ phase difference between the $o$- and $e$-components. Circular polarization requires equal amplitudes ($E_0\cos\theta = E_0\sin\theta$), which occurs at $\theta = 45^\circ$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Oscillations, Waves and Optics (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In a Michelson interferometer illuminated by monochromatic light of wavelength $\lambda$, one of the mirrors is translated by a distance $d = 5\lambda$. The number of circular fringes that cross the center of the field of view is
questions.explanationEn: Translating a mirror by $d$ changes the optical path difference by $2d$. The number of fringes shifted is $N = \frac{2d}{\lambda} = \frac{2(5\lambda)}{\lambda} = 10$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Oscillations, Waves and Optics (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In a Fraunhofer double-slit diffraction pattern, if the center-to-center slit separation $d$ is three times the individual slit width $a$ ($d = 3a$), which interference principal maxima are missing?
questions.explanationEn: Missing orders occur when an interference maximum ($d\sin\theta = m\lambda$) coincides with a single-slit diffraction minimum ($a\sin\theta = p\lambda$), giving $m = \frac{d}{a}p = 3p$, i.e., $m = \pm 3, \pm 6, \pm 9, \dots$

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Oscillations, Waves and Optics (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: An open organ pipe of length $L$ and a closed organ pipe (closed at one end) of length $L/2$ are filled with the same gas at the same temperature. Neglecting end corrections, the ratio of the fundamental frequency of the open pipe to that of the closed pipe is
questions.explanationEn: For an open pipe of length $L$, $f_{\text{open}} = \frac{v}{2L}$. For a closed pipe of length $L/2$, $f_{\text{closed}} = \frac{v}{4(L/2)} = \frac{v}{2L}$. Hence their ratio is $1$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Oscillations, Waves and Optics (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: An aqueous sucrose solution of concentration $0.15\text{ g/cm}^3$ is placed in a polarimeter tube of length $20\text{ cm}$. If the specific rotation of sucrose at the operating wavelength is $66^\circ\text{ dm}^{-1}(\text{g/cm}^3)^{-1}$, the observed optical rotation is
questions.explanationEn: The tube length in decimeters is $l = 20\text{ cm} = 2.0\text{ dm}$. Optical rotation is $\theta = [\alpha] l c = 66 \times 2.0 \times 0.15 = 19.8^\circ$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Oscillations, Waves and Optics (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Electromagnetic waves in a cold unmagnetized plasma obey the dispersion relation $\omega^2 = \omega_p^2 + c^2 k^2$, where $\omega_p$ is the plasma frequency and $c$ is the speed of light in vacuum. For $\omega > \omega_p$, the product of the phase velocity $v_p$ and the group velocity $v_g$ is
questions.explanationEn: Differentiating $\omega^2 = \omega_p^2 + c^2 k^2$ with respect to $k$ gives $2\omega \frac{d\omega}{dk} = 2c^2 k \implies \left(\frac{\omega}{k}\right)\left(\frac{d\omega}{dk}\right) = v_p v_g = c^2$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Oscillations, Waves and Optics (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A stationary ultrasonic source emits waves of frequency $f_0$ toward a flat reflector moving directly toward the source at speed $u < c_s$, where $c_s$ is the speed of sound in air. The frequency of the reflected wave detected back at the source is
questions.explanationEn: The moving reflector acts first as an approaching receiver detecting $f_1 = f_0\frac{c_s + u}{c_s}$, and then as an approaching source re-emitting $f_1$, so the stationary detector receives $f_2 = f_1 \frac{c_s}{c_s - u} = f_0 \frac{c_s + u}{c_s - u}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Oscillations, Waves and Optics (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A critically damped oscillator of mass $m = 2\text{ kg}$ and spring constant $k = 18\text{ N/m}$ starts from equilibrium $x(0) = 0$ with initial velocity $v(0) = 6\text{ m/s}$. The maximum displacement reached by the mass is
questions.explanationEn: Here $\omega_0 = \sqrt{k/m} = \sqrt{18/2} = 3\text{ rad/s}$. For critical damping ($\gamma = \omega_0 = 3\text{ s}^{-1}$) with $x(0) = 0$ and $\dot{x}(0) = 6$, the solution is $x(t) = 6t e^{-3t}$. Setting $\dot{x}(t) = 6(1 - 3t)e^{-3t} = 0$ gives $t = \frac{1}{3}\text{ s}$, where $x_{\max} = 6\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)e^{-1} = \frac{2}{e}\text{ m}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Oscillations, Waves and Optics (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: When right-handed circularly polarized light passes normally through an ideal half-wave plate, the emergent light is
optionsEn: linearly polarized along the fast axis
linearly polarized at $45^\circ$ to the fast axis
questions.explanationEn: A half-wave plate adds a phase shift of $\pi$ to one orthogonal component relative to the other, changing the relative phase from $+\pi/2$ to $-\pi/2$ (or vice versa) while preserving equal amplitudes. This reverses the handedness from right-handed to left-handed circular polarization.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Oscillations, Waves and Optics (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In a standard Young's double-slit experiment with slit separation $d$, screen distance $D \gg d$, and monochromatic light of wavelength $\lambda$, which of the following statements is/are correct?
optionsEn: If one slit is covered with a neutral filter that reduces its intensity to one-fourth of the other slit, the ratio $I_{\max}/I_{\min}$ becomes $9$
If white light is used instead of monochromatic light, the central fringe at zero path difference is white
If two independent identical sodium lamps illuminate the two slits separately, stationary interference fringes are still observed on the screen
Increasing the slit separation $d$ decreases the fringe width $\beta$
questions.explanationEn: If $I_2 = I_1/4$, then $A_2 = A_1/2$, so $I_{\max}/I_{\min} = (1 + 1/2)^2 / (1 - 1/2)^2 = 9$ (True). At zero path difference, all wavelengths interfere constructively, forming a white central fringe (True). Since $\beta = \lambda D / d$, increasing $d$ decreases $\beta$ (True). Independent thermal sources are mutually incoherent, so no stationary fringes form (False).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Oscillations, Waves and Optics (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A plane electromagnetic wave travels from a denser dielectric medium of refractive index $n_1 = 2.0$ toward air ($n_2 = 1.0$). Let $\theta_c$ be the critical angle for total internal reflection and $\theta_B$ be the internal Brewster angle. Which of the following statements is/are correct?
optionsEn: At incidence angle $\theta = \theta_B$, the reflected ray and refracted ray are perpendicular to each other
Total internal reflection occurs for all incidence angles $\theta > \theta_B$
questions.explanationEn: $\sin\theta_c = n_2/n_1 = 0.5 \implies \theta_c = 30^\circ$ (True). $\tan\theta_B = n_2/n_1 = 0.5 \implies \theta_B \approx 26.57^\circ < 30^\circ$ (True). At $\theta_B$, reflected and refracted rays are always orthogonal (True). TIR only occurs for $\theta > \theta_c$, not for $\theta_B < \theta < \theta_c$ (False).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Oscillations, Waves and Optics (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: For a wave propagating in a dispersive medium with dispersion relation $\omega(k)$ (where $k = 2\pi/\lambda$), which of the following relations between group velocity $v_g$ and phase velocity $v_p$ is/are always valid?
optionsEn: In a medium with normal dispersion ($\frac{dn}{d\lambda} < 0$), $v_g < v_p$
questions.explanationEn: Since $\omega = k v_p$, $v_g = \frac{d(k v_p)}{dk} = v_p + k\frac{dv_p}{dk}$ (True). Using $k = 2\pi/\lambda$, $k\frac{d}{dk} = -\lambda\frac{d}{d\lambda}$, so $v_g = v_p - \lambda\frac{dv_p}{d\lambda}$ (True). With $v_p = c/n$, $\frac{dv_p}{d\lambda} = -\frac{c}{n^2}\frac{dn}{d\lambda} > 0$ for normal dispersion, hence $v_g < v_p$ (True). In plasmas/waveguides $v_p > c$ while $v_g = c^2/v_p < c$ (False).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Oscillations, Waves and Optics (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A monochromatic light ray passes through a glass prism of apex angle $A$ and refractive index $n$ placed in air. At the condition of minimum deviation $\delta_m$, which of the following statements is/are correct?
optionsEn: The angle of incidence equals the angle of emergence ($i_1 = i_2$)
The deviation angle $\delta_m$ is independent of the wavelength of light
The ray inside the prism travels symmetrically with $r_1 = r_2 = A/2$
questions.explanationEn: At minimum deviation, the path is symmetric: $i_1 = i_2 = (A + \delta_m)/2$ and $r_1 = r_2 = A/2$, yielding $n = \frac{\sin[(A + \delta_m)/2]}{\sin(A/2)}$ (all three True). Because glass is dispersive ($n$ depends on $\lambda$), $\delta_m$ depends on wavelength (False).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Oscillations, Waves and Optics (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: An oil-immersion microscope objective has a numerical aperture $\text{NA} = 1.22$ and uses light of vacuum wavelength $500\text{ nm}$. Using the Rayleigh criterion $d_{\min} = \frac{0.61\lambda}{\text{NA}}$, the minimum resolvable distance between two point objects is ______ $\text{nm}$. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: Directly substituting gives $d_{\min} = \frac{0.61 \times 500\text{ nm}}{1.22} = 250\text{ nm}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Oscillations, Waves and Optics (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A glass lens ($n_g = 1.52$) is coated with a thin layer of $\text{MgF}_2$ ($n_c = 1.38$) to eliminate reflection at normal incidence for light of vacuum wavelength $552\text{ nm}$. The minimum thickness of the coating is ______ $\text{nm}$. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: Since $n_{\text{air}} < n_c < n_g$, both reflections undergo a $\pi$ phase shift. Destructive interference in reflection requires $2n_c t = \frac{\lambda}{2} \implies t = \frac{\lambda}{4n_c} = \frac{552}{4 \times 1.38} = 100\text{ nm}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Oscillations, Waves and Optics (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Unpolarized light in air is incident on a transparent dielectric plate of refractive index $1.48$. The Brewster angle for external reflection is ______ degrees. (Round off to 2 decimal places)
questions.explanationEn: By Brewster's law, $\theta_B = \tan^{-1}(n) = \tan^{-1}(1.48) \approx 55.95^\circ$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Oscillations, Waves and Optics (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In a Young's double-slit experiment, the slit separation is $0.5\text{ mm}$, the screen is placed $2.0\text{ m}$ away, and light of wavelength $550\text{ nm}$ is used. The fringe width on the screen is ______ $\text{mm}$. (Round off to 1 decimal place)
questions.explanationEn: The fringe width is $\beta = \frac{\lambda D}{d} = \frac{550 \times 10^{-9} \times 2.0}{0.5 \times 10^{-3}} = 2.2 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m} = 2.2\text{ mm}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Oscillations, Waves and Optics (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A point object is placed $18\text{ cm}$ in front of a concave spherical mirror of radius of curvature $24\text{ cm}$. The distance of the real image from the pole of the mirror is ______ $\text{cm}$. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: The focal length is $f = -R/2 = -12\text{ cm}$. By the mirror formula $\frac{1}{v} + \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f}$ with $u = -18\text{ cm}$, $\frac{1}{v} = -\frac{1}{12} + \frac{1}{18} = -\frac{1}{36}\text{ cm}^{-1}$, so the real image forms at $36\text{ cm}$ in front of the mirror.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Oscillations, Waves and Optics (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A block of mass $1\text{ kg}$ is attached to a spring of force constant $100\text{ N/m}$ and moves in a medium exerting a viscous damping force $F_d = -12v$ (in SI units). The damped angular frequency $\omega_d$ of its oscillations is ______ $\text{rad/s}$. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: Here $\omega_0^2 = \frac{k}{m} = 100\text{ s}^{-2}$ and $\gamma = \frac{b}{2m} = \frac{12}{2} = 6\text{ s}^{-1}$. Thus $\omega_d = \sqrt{\omega_0^2 - \gamma^2} = \sqrt{100 - 36} = 8\text{ rad/s}$.
